analysis:
The PR plumbs a new optional stopStringScope (CBv2StopStringScope?) through three paths. ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope(modelId:modelType:) in EngineV2SlotFactory.swift (patch line ~574) supplies it. EngineV2Factory.makeBridge (EngineV2Config.swift lines 157, 208) forwards it. EngineV2Bridge stores it as an immutable let (EngineV2Bridge.swift lines 109-111, 374, 435). In the supplied evidence the stored value is not read anywhere. Consumption in submission or translation code is outside this batch, so no enforcement behavior is visible here.

Security-relevant observations:
- The change is data plumbing only. It adds no network, crypto, key, attestation, authorization, or storage surface.
- It does not alter the prefix-cache construction or release paths (T-041), SSD cache wiring, or KV budget handling. The surrounding ssdPrefixCache and ssdHybridCheckpointStore initialization in EngineV2Bridge.swift lines 457-517 is unchanged.
- Stop-string scope only restricts where client-supplied stop strings match generated text. Any effect would be on output truncation correctness, not on the trust boundaries TB-002, TB-007 or TB-011. The default of nil preserves the existing whole-text matching behavior.
- No new telemetry, logging, or plaintext exposure of prompts is introduced.

Residual question for integration: confirm that the downstream request translation (not supplied) passes the scope into CBv2 stop-string matching and does not leak the prompt in logs. This is a correctness question, not a security one. The ModelEOSPolicy implementation is also not visible, so I cannot confirm the scope values are safe.
